Book I

Patrons

Three patrons are catalogued here: appetite and fracture, schedule and return, and ritualized perfection through needlework and occult craft.

Patron · The Demogorgon

The Two-Headed Prince

Dual-mind chassis · every feature reads or rewrites whether your alter ego is Suppressed or Manifested.
▸
Otherworldly Patron

The Demogorgon

A pact written in two hands at once. One head names every threat; the other promises every survival. You ride the seam between them, and the seam learns your name.

1st levelExpanded Spell List

Expanded Spell List

The two-headed prince adds his preferred dominations to your spell list.

1stCommandCompelled Duel
2ndTasha's Mind WhipBlur
3rdHasteBlink
4thConfusionFreedom of Movement
5thGeasTelekinesis
1st levelFocus-chassis

Fractured Psyche

Two minds wear one skull; the floor between them keeps shifting.

You have two alter egos: Manifested and Suppressed. As a Bonus Action on your turn, you can switch your alter ego to Suppressed, which lasts until you end it (no action required), until you are incapacitated, or until you take damage and fail a Constitution saving throw (DC 10 or half the damage taken, whichever is higher). Otherwise, your alter ego is Manifested.
1st levelSame-beat cost

Psychic Breach

When their will splinters, yours leans through the crack.

When a creature fails a saving throw against one of your spells, and that saving throw adds its Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma modifier, you can expend one Hit Die and roll it, producing one of the following effects according to your current state. When you reach 10th level in this class, you can expend two Hit Dice and roll them instead.

Manifested. You gain temporary hit points equal to the number rolled.
Suppressed. The creature takes psychic damage equal to the number rolled.
1st levelSpell-list adapter

Cult Indoctrination

A feature of the two-headed pact.

You learn the true strike cantrip and one cantrip of your choice from mind sliver or vicious mockery. These cantrips count as warlock cantrips for you and don't count against your number of cantrips known.
6th levelSocial pressure

Mental Schemer

A feature of the two-headed pact.

You learn one spell of your choice: charm person or cause fear. It doesn't count against your number of spells known. Additionally, you can take the Influence action as a bonus action.
10th levelMental evasion

Ragged Bastion

A feature of the two-headed pact.

When you fail an Intelligence, Wisdom, or Charisma saving throw, you can use your reaction to expend one Hit Die and roll it, adding the number rolled to the saving throw, potentially turning the failure into a success. If you succeed on the saving throw in this way, damage you take from that effect until the end of the turn doesn't break your concentration.
14th levelState inversion

Pandemonium of Two Heads

A feature of the two-headed pact.

As an Action, you can project your presence into the minds of all creatures within 30 feet of you until the end of your next turn. While your alter ego is Manifested, any creature within 30 feet of you that is frightened of you always knows your exact location, and you always know its exact location. While your alter ego is Suppressed, any creature within 30 feet of you that is charmed by you cannot perceive you with any of their senses.

The Clockwork Cosmos

Otherworldly Patron

The Machine

Not a god so much as a schedule. The Machine offers no mercy and no omen; it grants cadence, accounting, and the terrible serenity of a wheel that never misses its tooth.

1st levelExpanded Spell List

Expanded Spell List

Each spell is a tooth on the wheel.

LevelSpell 1Spell 2
1stAbsorb ElementsGrease
2ndFind TrapsTasha's Wristpocket
3rdElemental WeaponTiny Servant
4thStoneskinFabricate
5thAnimate ObjectsCreation
1st levelSpecialty

Graduated Technomancer

Choose your discipline within the great engine.

At 1st level, choose one of the following specialties:

Electrics. You gain proficiency with tinker's tools, and you learn the shocking grasp cantrip. It counts as a warlock cantrip for you and doesn't count against your number of cantrips known.

Mechanics. You gain proficiency with smith's tools, and you learn the mending and prestidigitation cantrips. They count as warlock cantrips for you and don't count against your number of cantrips known.
6th levelResource recursion

Ledger Adjustment

The Machine never refunds a debt; it merely schedules its return.

When you finish a short rest, you can inscribe one expended warlock spell slot on the Machine's ledger. Before you finish a long rest, when you cast a warlock spell, you can erase one inscribed slot to treat that casting as though the slot were one level higher than normal, to a maximum of 5th level. You can keep no more than three inscribed slots on the ledger at one time, and all remaining entries vanish when you finish a long rest.
10th levelTurn scheduling

Cosmic Latency

The wheel can force a moment to wait for its proper tooth.

When a creature you can see within 60 feet would make an attack roll, ability check, or saving throw, you can use your reaction to delay that roll until the start of its next turn. During the delay, the creature can't take reactions, and if it willingly moves more than 10 feet before the delayed roll resolves, the roll is lost. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.
14th levelPredestination engine

Final Tooth

For one round, the wheel stops guessing and simply remembers.

As an action, you lock the next round into the Machine's preferred sequence. Until the end of your next turn, once on each creature's turn, you can replace one attack roll, ability check, or saving throw made by a creature you can see within 60 feet with a result of 10 before modifiers. A creature whose result you replace glimmers with clockwork light until the effect ends. Once you use this feature, you can't do so again until you finish a long rest.

The Perfect Design

A gestalt will born from collective obsession with flawless craft. Its warlocks become living needles: tailors of fate, courtly specialists, and occult artisans who rewrite reality one precise puncture at a time.

Expanded Spell List

Neophyte's Inspirational Knowledge

True mastery is measured by the exactness of the counsel you impart.

You learn the Guidance cantrip. It counts as a warlock cantrip for you, but it doesn't count against your number of cantrips known.

When you cast it, you can restrict its benefit to a single skill or tool with which you are proficient. When you do so, the target adds your Charisma bonus to the ability check in addition to the spell's d4, and the same creature can't benefit from your Guidance spell again before it finishes a Long Rest.
1st levelCalculated tempo

Methodical Execution

Every feint, assist, and held breath is an angle of attack.

You learn the True Strike cantrip, but it doesn't count against your number of cantrips known.

When you cast it, or when you take the Help action to aid a creature you can see, or Ready an action keyed to trigger on the turn of a creature you can see, you gain Advantage on the next d20 Roll you make before the start of your next turn.
6th levelCourtly specialization

Perfect Design

Masterpiece craft is your social credential and your spellcasting instrument.

You gain tool proficiencies from one of the following courtly specializations of your choice:

Fashionist. Disguise kit and your choice of leatherworker's tools or weaver's tools.
Impressionist. Forgery kit and your choice of calligrapher's supplies or painter's supplies.
Instrumentalist. Thieves' tools and your choice of jeweler's tools or tinker's tools.

While holding any tool granted by this feature, you can use it as a spellcasting focus for your warlock spells.
6th levelBallistic geometry

Unerring Vector

Force is merely a blunt instrument until sharpened to a needle's point.

You learn Jim's Magic Missile. It counts as a warlock spell for you, doesn't count against your number of spells known, and doesn't require its material component when you cast it.

When you cast Jim's Magic Missile or Eldritch Blast, you can change the spell's damage type from Force to Piercing.
10th levelAsymptotic floor

Converging Perfection

At the edge of failure, the design folds back toward flawlessness.

When you roll a 1 on a d20 Test, you can treat the roll as a 19 instead. You can use this feature a number of times equal to your Proficiency Bonus, and you regain all expended uses when you finish a Long Rest.
14th levelRadiant puncture apex

Zenith of the Golden Ratio

Where the smallest needle-prick lands, golden radiance erupts along the seam.

When you deal Piercing damage to a target with an attack, the target takes an extra 1d10 Radiant damage for each of the attack's Piercing damage dice that rolls a 1.
Book II

Pact Boons

Each boon is treated here as an invocation district: a promise, a load-bearing fantasy, and a track of workings that sharpen it.
▸

Pact Boons · canonical shell

The Noosphere routes each boon through a short bespoke invocation suite. This page now treats the boons as stable districts of the codex, even when individual workings inside them are still being tuned.

Track❖ Pact of the TomeThe grimoire track favours stolen language, ritual elasticity, and invocations that make knowledge feel alive, hungry, and expensive.
Track⛓ Pact of the ChainThe familiar track centres on divided agency: scouting, sabotage, relay-casting, and bargains that let the servant become a witness.
Track⚔ Pact of the BladeThe weapon track sharpens threat geometry, duelling pressure, and invocations that turn a summoned armament into a sentence the battlefield must finish reading.
Track◈ Pact of the TalismanThe token track deals in rebound luck, carried vows, and invocations that let failure glance off the bearer and return marked for collection.

Implementation rule for the next codex pass: each boon should read as a complete play promise before its dedicated invocation rail is expanded.

Arachnidian Metamorphosis

You move where webs command and walls remember your name.The blade-bearer never stays caught for long.

Prerequisite. Ability to cast Spider Climb.

Effect:

When you expend a spell slot to cast Spider Climb, for its duration Difficult Terrain and crawling don’t cost you extra movement, and you have Advantage on saving throws to avoid the Grappled and Restrained conditions and on ability checks to escape them.
Design Audit★★★★· ⚡⚡··· 🚨····

Closest Analogues ★★★★·

Now matches the designer's spec: mobility plus grapple and restraint resistance, gated to Pact of the Blade, which gives it a different gating axis from Weaver's Knack (spell access) so the two no longer unlock together.

Insight ⚡⚡···

RAW: 2024 grapple escape uses an ability check, not a saving throw, so a saves-only clause would cover avoiding a grapple but not escaping one. Covering both checks and saves makes "avoid being and staying" grappled actually work. RAT: a melee warlock who is never pinned down reads as a spider, not a fly.

Patch 🚨····

Removed from the prior text: "ignore movement restrictions imposed by webs." Restore it if a web-walking Blade warlock is intended; the web-sense clause now lives on Arachnidian Senses.

Verdict

Table-ready.

Lens 49: Elegance
❖

Arcane Blueprints

Every glyph is a blueprint; every blueprint remembers a spell.The circle-maker learns to fold a stored spell into the lines themselves.

Prerequisite. Sacred Geometry invocation, proficiency in Arcana or with painter's supplies.

Effect:

You learn Glyph of Warding. It counts as a Warlock spell for you and doesn't count against the number of spells you know. Choose one spell of 3rd level or lower from any class’s spell list. When you cast Glyph of Warding and choose its Spell Glyph option, you can store that spell in the glyph as though you had it prepared. You can take this invocation more than once, choosing a different spell each time.
Design Audit★★★·· ⚡⚡⚡·· 🚨····

Closest Analogues ★★★··

A Rewarded Pursue card: the first take grants Glyph of Warding itself; every retake, once Glyph is already known, grants a new glyph-storable spell instead. The branch is what makes retaking meaningful rather than a flat repeat.

Insight ⚡⚡⚡··

RAS: the chosen off-list spell is usable only through the glyph, so it widens what the warlock can prepare in advance without widening what they can cast on the spot. Depth: chains off Sacred Geometry at depth one, and nothing chains off this card, so the prerequisite ceiling holds. RAE: Glyph of Warding's 200 gp component and 1-hour cast keep every stored spell a planned investment.

Patch 🚨····

Watch item: repeated takes let a Tome warlock bank several off-list 3rd-level spells. The 200 gp per glyph and one-hour cast are the governor; if a table finds it too strong, cap takes at three.

Verdict

Table-ready, with a named watch item rather than a hidden one.

Audited Execution

You pre-authorize allied success on a single decisive roll.Prepared precision becomes a team spike.

Prerequisite. 9th level, the Perfect Design patron.

Effect:

As an Action, you can take the Ready action, choosing a willing ally that can see or hear you as the trigger: the ally rolling a d20. When the trigger occurs, you can take your readied Reaction to turn that d20 roll into a 19, after seeing the roll but before the DM says whether it succeeds. Once you use this feature, you can't use it again until you finish a Short or Long Rest.
Design Audit★★★★· ⚡⚡⚡·· ·····

Closest Analogues ★★★★·

RAG: the original had no rest limiter on an effect that turns an ally's roll into a guaranteed natural 19 — well-costed for a single use, but nothing stopped it firing every round, all day. The short-rest recharge closes that without touching the action-and-reaction cost, which was already sound.

Insight ⚡⚡⚡··

RAA: short rest rather than long rest keeps this tied to the warlock's own existing Pact Magic rhythm instead of bottlenecking it to once per adventuring day, matching the cadence of the resource it's built alongside.

Patch ·····

None outstanding.

Verdict

Table-ready.

Body Jewelry

Your talisman is implanted, not worn, and hardens into couture armor.Defense is ritual bodywork.

Prerequisite. Pact of the Talisman feature.

Effect:

While the wearer of your talisman is affected by your Mage Armor, its base AC becomes your spell save DC instead of 13 plus its Dexterity modifier, and your talisman can't be removed from the wearer for the spell's duration.
Design Audit★★★★★ ⚡⚡··· ·····

Closest Analogues ★★★★★

RAS: piggybacking on Mage Armor's own casting cost, duration, and dons-armor cutoff means this needs no new duration system or tracker of its own — a direct application of the Book of Knowledge's veto against inventing currencies the game already provides.

Insight ⚡⚡···

RAD: the prior 13+Charisma formula plateaus the moment Charisma caps, usually by level 4–8, and then sits dead for the rest of the character's career. Spell Save DC keeps climbing every time proficiency bonus does — levels 5, 9, 13, 17 all push it further. The curve is better, not just the wording.

Patch ·····

None outstanding. Open item: whether Mage Armor is actually warlock-castable in this ecosystem hasn't been confirmed — this invocation is inert without it.

Verdict

Table-ready and structurally the strongest fix of this entire sprint — simpler design that's also a better curve, not a tradeoff between the two.

Embrace the Raging Baboon

A working that unfastens copper-tasting the gait, then balances the index against its echo. Read the print only if the print is willing.Any pact can carry this working — a stored spell drunk down to fund the trick.

Prerequisite. 9th level, the Demogorgon patron.

Design Audit★★★★· ⚡⚡··· 🚨🚨···

Designer decision

The alignment lock is permanent on purpose. Every other invocation in this compendium can be swapped out; this one is the bargain that can't be undone, and that irreversibility is the whole of its cost.

Insight

RAE: a player choosing this should feel the weight of a one-way door, so the table should raise it in session zero rather than let it be taken casually at level-up. RAG: because no effect reverses it, there is nothing for a DM to adjudicate later.

Verdict

Table-ready as a deliberate outlier. Flagged in the full-set audit as the heaviest commitment in the set and kept by design.

Closest Analogues ★★★★·

RAW: the prior effect required "concentrating on true strike" as its entire trigger condition — a state that doesn't exist under 2024 rules, where True Strike is Instantaneous with no concentration component at all. Found via a full-set scan for the same edition assumption already confirmed in Colosseum's Champion and Vengeful Megalomaniac.

Insight ⚡⚡···

RAT: anchoring the advantage to the hit itself, with a bounded "until the end of your next turn" window, preserves the exact fantasy — mark a target with a precision cantrip, then punish them for fleeing — while resting on something that actually exists in the current rules instead of a nonexistent ongoing state.

Patch ·····

None outstanding.

Verdict

Table-ready. Fourth confirmed instance of this compendium's True-Strike-as-concentration assumption, all four now resolved.

RAS: this is a parallelism violation in the strictest Book of Knowledge sense — four cards doing the same job at two different price points, with the difference explainable only by which card happened to get written last. Removing it isn't a nerf, it's closing a gap between sibling cards that should never have opened.

Table-ready. Consistent with its three sibling cards in cost, structure, and framing.

Iron Maiden's Embrace

You become a golden sarcophagus and sentence a target to shared suffering.Containment and reflection merge.

Prerequisite. Mystic Arcanum (6th level), the Perfect Design patron.

Effect:

As a Bonus Action while you are Grappling a creature, you can expend one use of your Mystic Arcanum (6th level), instead of casting its chosen spell, to transmute yourself into a golden iron maiden that engulfs one creature you are Grappling until the start of your next turn. For that duration, you have the Petrified condition, and the engulfed creature has the Blinded and Restrained conditions, has Total Cover against effects from outside you, takes the same damage you take (after your Resistances) while you also take it, can't regain Hit Points, and can't teleport.
Design Audit★★★★· ⚡⚡⚡·· ·····

Closest Analogues ★★★★·

The rebuilt version gates the transformation behind an already-successful grapple instead of a second, independent Strength save — the same target that already failed to escape your grip doesn't get re-tested against a different mechanic to be trapped by it. That's RAA: the fantasy resolves in one roll the fiction already earned, not two.

Insight ⚡⚡⚡··

RAT: becoming a coffin around a foe you're already holding reads as an escalation of the grapple, not a separate spell effect layered on top — the mechanic expresses the fantasy directly. RAS: "total cover" reuses an existing keyed term instead of inventing bespoke no-target language, and the grapple gate reuses an existing action-economy system instead of adding a new save DC to track. RAW: capping duration at "until the start of your next turn" removes the cross-round state tracking the original's flat 1-minute duration required — a direct Book of Knowledge Veto Wall violation in the prior version, now closed.

Patch ·····

None outstanding. The self-petrification and can't-regain-hit-points clauses are real, felt costs matching a 7th-tier Arcanum price point.

Verdict

Table-ready. Every clause in the current text is load-bearing; nothing here needs trimming or re-costing.

Design Audit★★★★· ⚡⚡⚡·· ·····

Closest Analogues ★★★★·

RAW: the original granted four full spells (ensnaring strike, entangle, web, spider climb) with no exemption from the warlock's Spells Known cap — the same gap independently found in Tome of Far Realms and Firefighter's Codex. Spider Climb moves from granted-spell to prerequisite-gate here, which frees the remaining structure for a genuine choice (one of two) plus a guaranteed third, rather than a flat four-spell dump.

Insight ⚡⚡⚡··

RAS: the prerequisite dropped the Pact of the Blade and character-level gates the original carried — neither was load-bearing, since the spider-silk fantasy doesn't require a weapon bond. RAD: this is objectively more generous in real terms (three of four spells now cost nothing against Spells Known) while using less text than the original.

Patch ·····

None outstanding.

Verdict

Table-ready. All four original spells remain reachable through this invocation; only the cost accounting changed.

Design Audit★★★★· ⚡⚡··· ·····

Closest Analogues ★★★★·

Replaces the prior version (Symbol cast as an action for a 7th-tier Arcanum plus exhaustion) with the designer's own redesign. Magic Circle lacks the ritual tag in both the 2014 and 2024 rules, so the ritual clause is a real grant, not a restatement.

Insight ⚡⚡···

RAT: sacred geometry expressed as slow, deliberate circle-drawing rather than instant catastrophe. RAS: gating on mason's tools or Religion ties the rite to the character's actual craft instead of a patron, which is why the card is now open to every patron. RAE: a ritual cast costs ten extra minutes, never a slot, so the power lands in preparation rather than combat. Synergy: Epitaph already requires the ability to cast magic circle; this card is now a natural route into it with no added prerequisite depth.

Patch ·····

None outstanding. The old Symbol-as-an-action identity is retired, not renamed; it can return as its own card if wanted.

Verdict

Table-ready. A patron-open utility rite with a clear cost (time) and a clean single grant.

Design Audit★★★·· ⚡⚡··· ·····

Closest Analogues ★★★··

Grants five full spells at once — more than any other single "add to spell list" card in this compendium (most grant one to three). Weaver's Knack and Firefighter's Codex both faced the identical gap: multi-spell grants with no stated exemption from a warlock's Spells Known cap, discovered and fixed in two earlier sprints.

Insight ⚡⚡···

RAW: without an explicit "doesn't count against spells known" clause, the base rule for "add to spell list" language is that the character still pays their normal Spells Known cost to actually learn each one — meaning this card, as originally written, could cost a player five of their limited known-spell slots just to gain access, a steep and almost certainly unintended tax for a single 5th-level invocation. RAS: adding the clause brings this in line with the compendium's own now-established convention for multi-spell grants rather than leaving it a silent, more expensive outlier.

Patch ·····

None outstanding.

Verdict

Table-ready. Five spells is still a lot for one invocation to grant compared to its siblings, but that's a scope choice, not a rules gap — worth a second look if it ever needs trimming, not a hard block now.

Patterns

What the corpus is doing right and where it strains.
▸

This board is a snapshot of the original automated audit of the 176-invocation set, taken before the manual rules-as-written review. That review has since covered all 205 invocations and the 15 subclass features, and closed seven systemic defect patterns across the set; the scores below describe the earlier snapshot, not the current text.

176Invocations
2.0Uniqueness
1.8Insight
9High Pressure
Pros

Strong variable exploration

The set explores existing 5e variables through patron gates, pact gates, Hit Dice, Exhaustion, conditions, and familiar forms.

Cons

High-tier replacement risk

9 cards score 4+ power pressure; 20 need urgent patching where high-level spells or absolute wording bypass scarcity.

Math

Scoring model

Power = scope + cadence + action timing + replacement risk - limiter. Mean power 1.8/5, mean patch urgency 2.1/5.

MDA

Predicted experience

Mechanics produce mastery/control fantasy; dynamics push toward forced movement, condition leverage, and spell-list optimization.

Book VI

Design Grammar

Fifteen card patterns plus the Bookbound Procedure doctrine.
▸

Ten rounds of your rewrites converge on a small set of repeatable sentences. Each pattern below has one fixed template and one cost, and lists every card that uses it. Gold chips are your rewrites; plain chips were brought into line with them. Click a chip to jump to the card.

  1. Capability gates over identity gates. A prerequisite names what the card needs in order to work (a spell, a pact, a proficiency). A patron is required only when the card is that patron’s signature.
  2. Action economy first, rest counters for sustained effects. A Reaction, Bonus Action or Concentration is the default limit. A rest counter is added only when an effect lasts a minute or more.
  3. Every tax is named once. Each pattern has exactly one cost (slot, Exhaustion, Reaction, 1 minute, Arcanum). A card never pays two taxes of the same kind.
  4. Riders need a real slot. A rider that adds power to a leveled spell triggers only when a spell slot is expended; ritual and cosmetic riders stay ungated.
  5. Prerequisites are context. A card is read with its prerequisites already in play: Pact of the Chain means the familiar can attack, Pact of the Tome means the Book of Shadows is at hand, and a swapped spell may already be on the Warlock list.
  6. Never re-impose the base rules. If the core rules already limit something (the ability check for a high-level Spell Scroll, a familiar attacking only through Pact of the Chain), a card doesn’t add a second limit or restate the first.
  7. Split by fantasy, not by power. Two cards may share a template when they carry different fantasies (the four Initiative Openers each pair a different two skills and two spells). Splitting keeps each invocation one idea instead of a bloated package; audits call such siblings overlaps, never collisions.
  8. Parametric over enumerated. A form list is a filter (creature type, Challenge Rating, size), not a roster of names, so any bestiary works and the list never goes stale.
  9. Write in 2024 terms. Designer intent is kept and translated into 2024 rules: spells known become “always prepared”, grapple attacks become a save DC, natural weapons become attacks, and actions are named (Magic, Search, Study, Influence).
  10. Midnight for crafted magic, Long Rest for characters. Jewelry, tattoos, letters and stored spells you craft end at midnight, a fairytale clock; a warlock’s own features reset on a Long Rest.
  11. Link, don’t paste. Official items, creatures and downtime activities are linked, never re-described, so the codex can’t drift from the source.
  12. Level ladder 5 / 7 / 9 / 12 / 15. Level gates use the official invocation tiers, and a gate is dropped when another prerequisite (such as a Mystic Arcanum) already implies the level.
⚖

Arcanum Swap

G2

Spend a Mystic Arcanum on a named spell instead of its chosen spell, and pay 1 Exhaustion.

You can expend one use of your Mystic Arcanum (Nth level) to cast [Spell] at Nth level instead of its chosen spell. If you do, you gain 1 Exhaustion level.
Why
The Arcanum tier is a design lever. Most swapped spells are already Warlock spells, so a same-tier swap buys flexibility on the day (you didn’t have to pick that spell as your Arcanum) and a higher-tier swap buys an extra casting of a spell you could already pick. Either way it is a one-off, paid in the body.

Initiative Opener

G5

Act the moment Initiative is rolled, before anyone takes a turn.

When you roll Initiative, you can take a Reaction to take the Influence action, but only to make a Charisma ([Skill A] or [Skill B]) check. On a success against a hostile creature, it hesitates: it can't take Reactions until the start of its first turn. If you can cast [Spell A] or [Spell B], you can cast one of them instead as part of that same Reaction.
Why
The Reaction you spend is the one you would have held for the first round, so the opener costs tempo. Each opener gates on proficiency in one of its two skills and pairs them with two spells. Against a hostile creature, a successful check has a fixed result (no Reactions until its first turn), so the table never stalls deciding what Influence does in combat.

Your first-round Reaction

Familiar Reform

G6

Find Familiar can take a patron-flavoured form.

When you cast Find Familiar [or Flock of Familiars], the summoned spirits can assume the form of [Form]. Each spirit disappears when it drops to 0 Hit Points or after 1 hour.
Why
Base familiar rules are never restated, so a card states only what it changes. The forms are stronger than Find Familiar’s CR 0 beasts, so they are a loan: one hour, then you recast the ritual. That keeps them ungated by slots. Mount forms (a warhorse, a mule) are exempt, because travel is their job. Each patron pairs a Cohort (G6, weak form, 1 hour) with an Emissary (G4, strong form, Mystic Arcanum, 1 minute).

Spell & Steel

G12

Spell and pact weapon in the same turn.

When you [cast Spell / hit with a Melee Spell Attack], you can make one attack with your Pact Weapon [against that creature] as a Bonus Action.

Replacement form: When you take the Attack action on your turn, you can replace one of your attacks with [a spell attack].
Why
Pact of the Blade’s fantasy is weaving spell and steel. The Bonus Action (or the replaced attack) is the budget, so the card adds tempo options, not raw actions.
Tax
Your Bonus Action, or one attack
4 cardsHelix Of SoulsSpellweaving DervishSpiral of DeathThreatening Display
⇢

Bonus-Action Shift

G13

Take a named action as a Bonus Action.

[You / The creature] can take the [Search / Study / Help] action as a Bonus Action.
Why
Only the action’s cost changes, never its effect, so information and support actions get cheaper without adding a new effect to balance.
Tax
Your Bonus Action
4 cardsCoordinated MindsCriticist's EyesHunting PackWeb Stalker
♥

Hit Die Fuel

G14

Your Hit Point Dice pay for the effect.

[Trigger], you can expend one of your Hit Point Dice and roll it. [The effect uses the number rolled.]
Why
Hit Point Dice are the body’s currency: every die spent here is healing you won’t get on a Short Rest, so the cost limits itself and no rest counter is needed.
Tax
One Hit Point Die
5 cardsArtistic ObsessionCollide EgosFlesh-Stitching ArtistIntrusive MurmursVessel of Vitality
⟲

Reaction Cast

G15

A trigger lets you cast a spell you know as a Reaction.

When [trigger], you can take a Reaction to cast [Spell].
Why
The slot-paid twin of Arcanum Reaction (G3): the base rules already spend the slot, so the card names only the trigger. A Reaction is once per round, which keeps it from stacking.
Tax
Your Reaction (and the spell’s slot)
3 cardsDeceiving DecoyDesperate HibernationInsidious Mockery
✎

Bookbound Procedure

Tome

The book, page, letter, ink, or bookmark is the magical interface; the chosen procedure is the trigger, not decorative flavour.

[Write / Fold / Sign / Read / Draw / Open] + [book or page] → [effect] → [one clear limit or exit].
Why
Preserves Tome identity while letting each rite pay a different existing 5e cost. These bespoke workings use G8 prerequisite syntax, not a new universal resource.
Audit
Reject any rite that duplicates the existing scroll, glyph, page-swarm, or thought-extraction niches.
